sources.title: Cosmological constraints on curved quintessence

evidence.text: Model comparison uses χ²=-2 ln Lmax and AIC=2n-2 ln Lmax. Relative to curved ΛCDM, qCDM adds one parameter and CPL adds two. The authors call AIC simplistic and leave computationally expensive Bayesian-evidence comparisons unperformed.

sources.title: Is curvature-assisted quintessence observationally viable?

evidence.text: Bayesian MCMC parameter estimation using Planck CMB distance priors, a BAO compilation, and Pantheon+ supernovae. Four analyses combine fixed/free present curvature with fixed/free initial scalar velocity.

sources.title: Has DESI detected exponential quintessence?

evidence.text: The authors also compute AIC=χ²min+2n and BIC=χ²min+n ln N. Separately, they fit CPL and its quadratic/cubic extensions in (1−a) to the mean quintessence equation of state, holding w0=wϕ(0); these approximation exercises differ from fitting those parametrizations directly to observations.

sources.title: Constraining spatial curvature with priors from swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Numerical integration of an autonomous background system tracks radiation, matter and scalar evolution, with the Friedmann constraint eliminating the matter density variable. The authors explicitly do not perform a new fixed-point stability analysis.

sources.title: Cosmological constraints on curved quintessence

evidence.text: A modified CAMB implementation supplies cosmological evolution and observables. MCMC varies λ with seven cosmological parameters, using wide uniform priors, Cobaya and a Gelman–Rubin stopping value R-1=0.03. GetDist analyzes chains; Py-BOBYQA finds best-fit likelihoods.

sources.title: Cosmological constraints on curved quintessence

evidence.text: Autonomous first-order dynamical systems and fixed-point stability analysis characterize background trajectories. For the closed case, variables normalized using H̄=H√(1-Ωk) compactify the otherwise noncompact phase space; the fixed-point discussion restricts to expanding universes. The open-case analysis is summarized from prior work.

evidence.text: Covariant-derivative commutators are mapped to harmonic-oscillator algebra to obtain charged spectra; the index theorem supplies the flux-dependent degeneracy. A four-dimensional one-loop effective-potential calculation then gives the Casimir energy.

sources.title: Gaugino Condensates and D-terms from D7-branes

evidence.text: A Dirac index on the real two-dimensional intersection counts chiral bifundamentals. The imported Veneziano–Yankielowicz–Taylor description, with the gaugino bilinear integrated out, supplies the ADS superpotential used for the gauge-invariance comparison.

sources.title: Moduli stabilisation and de Sitter string vacua from magnetised D7 branes

evidence.text: The authors construct gauge-invariant Affleck–Dine–Seiberg superpotentials, integrate out sufficiently massive quarks, and minimise V_F+V_D using large-volume expansions and numerical examples.

sources.title: Moduli stabilization in (string) model building: Gauge fluxes and loops

evidence.text: The paper computes the flux potential both by reducing the six-dimensional gauge kinetic term and by identifying the gauged axionic isometry and its four-dimensional D-term. Agreement is presented as a consistency check within the calculation.

sources.title: Moduli stabilization in (string) model building: Gauge fluxes and loops

evidence.text: For stabilization, the authors first solve the KKLT-like S problem at f = 0 and t = 1, then approximate s by its resulting minimum while minimizing the flux-corrected t potential. Loop corrections are subsequently added to assess the displacement of the minimum.

sources.title: Gaugino Condensates and D-terms from D7-branes

evidence.text: Dimensional reduction of the bosonic DBI action, using calibration conditions and an expansion near supersymmetry, extracts the D-term and gauge coupling. Reduction of Chern–Simons couplings identifies axion gauging and checks relative signs through holomorphic gauge kinetic functions.
